paper_title: Measurement-induced entanglement and complexity in random constant-depth 2D quantum circuits (McGinley, 2025, arXiv)
core_reasoning_5:
\textbf{Claim.} For a fixed separating domain wall $W$, the trace-norm contribution of all spin configurations containing $W$ obeys
\[
\|X(I_W)\|_1\le \exp\left(\frac12(\log d'-S_W^{(2)})\right).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & I_W\text{ is the set of spin configurations containing the separating wall }W.\\
(P2) & X(I_W)=\sigma^{FC}\otimes\sigma^{W^+}\otimes\sum_r p_r|r\rangle\langle r|^{M_{F_A}}\otimes T_r.\\
(P3) & T_r:=(\Theta_{W^-}\otimes\Theta_A)[\sigma^{AW^-}_r],\quad \sum_r p_r=1,\quad p_r\ge 0.\\
(P4) & \|\sigma\|_1=1\text{ for every density matrix }\sigma,\text{ and }\|X\otimes Y\|_1=\|X\|_1\|Y\|_1.\\
(P5) & \|L\|_1\le \|\sigma^{-1/4}L\sigma^{-1/4}\|_2\text{ for every Hermitian }L\text{ and density matrix }\sigma.\\
(P6) & \text{There are modified maps }\widetilde\Theta_i,\widetilde\Theta_A\text{ such that }\\
     & \|T_r\|_1\le \|(\widetilde\Theta_{W^-}\otimes\widetilde\Theta_A)[\sigma^{AW^-}_r]\|_2.\\
(P7) & \|\widetilde\Theta_i[Y]\|_2\le \|Y\|_2\text{ for all }i\in W^-\text{ and all }Y.\\
(P8) & \|\widetilde\Theta_A[Y]\|_2\le \sqrt{d'}\|Y\|_2\text{ for all }Y.\\
(P9) & \|\Phi\otimes\Gamma\|_{2\to 2}=\|\Phi\|_{2\to 2}\|\Gamma\|_{2\to 2}.\\
(P10) & S_W^{(2)}:=-\log\operatorname{Tr}[(\sigma^{AW^-}_r)^2]\text{ is independent of }r.\\
(P11) & \|\omega\|_2:=\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(\omega^2)}\text{ for density matrices }\omega.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First reduce the norm of $X(I_W)$ to the norms of the $T_r$ terms:
\begin{align}
\|X(I_W)\|_1
&=\left\|\sigma^{FC}\otimes\sigma^{W^+}\otimes\sum_r p_r|r\rangle\langle r|\otimes T_r\right\|_1 && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=\sum_r p_r\|\sigma^{FC}\otimes\sigma^{W^+}\otimes T_r\|_1 && \text{orthogonal classical blocks}\\
&=\sum_r p_r\|T_r\|_1 && \text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}
For each $r$,
\begin{align}
\|T_r\|_1
&\le \|(\widetilde\Theta_{W^-}\otimes\widetilde\Theta_A)[\sigma^{AW^-}_r]\|_2 && \text{by (P6), derived from (P5)}\\
&\le \|\widetilde\Theta_{W^-}\otimes\widetilde\Theta_A\|_{2\to 2}\,\|\sigma^{AW^-}_r\|_2 && \text{definition of induced norm}\\
&=\left(\prod_{i\in W^-}\|\widetilde\Theta_i\|_{2\to 2}\right)\|\widetilde\Theta_A\|_{2\to 2}\,\|\sigma^{AW^-}_r\|_2 && \text{by (P9)}\\
&\le \sqrt{d'}\,\|\sigma^{AW^-}_r\|_2 && \text{by (P7) and (P8)}\\
&=\sqrt{d'}\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}[(\sigma^{AW^-}_r)^2]} && \text{by (P11)}\\
&=\sqrt{d'}\,\exp\left(-\frac12 S_W^{(2)}\right) && \text{by (P10)}\\
&=\exp\left(\frac12(\log d'-S_W^{(2)})\right). && \text{algebra}
\end{align}
Averaging over $r$ cannot increase this uniform bound:
\begin{align}
\|X(I_W)\|_1
&=\sum_r p_r\|T_r\|_1 && \text{from above}\\
&\le \sum_r p_r\exp\left(\frac12(\log d'-S_W^{(2)})\right) && \text{uniform bound}\\
&=\exp\left(\frac12(\log d'-S_W^{(2)})\right). && \text{since }\sum_r p_r=1
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\|X(I_W)\|_1\le \exp\left(\frac12(\log d'-S_W^{(2)})\right).}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\textbf{Claim.} If separating domain walls are weighted by $H[W]=S_W^{(2)}/2$, then the average distillation error satisfies
\[
\epsilon\le \sqrt{d'}\,Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}f(Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}),\qquad f(x):=\frac{e^x-1}{x}.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \mathcal W:=\operatorname{SAW}(\Lambda^*,A,C)\text{ is the set of self-avoiding separating walls from }A\text{ to }C.\\
(P2) & H[W]:=S_W^{(2)}/2.\\
(P3) & Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}:=\sum_{W\in\mathcal W}e^{-H[W]}.\\
(P4) & \text{For exactly }n\ge 1\text{ separating walls, Appendix-D inclusion-exclusion gives total contribution}\\
     & \text{at most }\sqrt{d'}\,Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}^n/n!.\\
(P5) & e^x-1=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}x^n/n!\text{ for every real }x.\\
(P6) & f(x):=(e^x-1)/x\text{ for }x>0.\\
(P7) & Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}>0.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Summing the contributions from all positive numbers of separating walls gives
\begin{align}
\epsilon
&\le \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sqrt{d'}\,\frac{Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}^n}{n!} && \text{by (P4)}\\
&=\sqrt{d'}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}^n}{n!} && \text{factor out }\sqrt{d'}\\
&=\sqrt{d'}\,(e^{Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}}-1) && \text{by (P5)}\\
&=\sqrt{d'}\,Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}\frac{e^{Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}}-1}{Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}} && \text{multiply and divide by }Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}>0\\
&=\sqrt{d'}\,Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}f(Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}). && \text{by (P6)}
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\epsilon\le \sqrt{d'}\,Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}f(Z_{\mathrm{SAW}}),\qquad f(x)=\frac{e^x-1}{x}.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_9:
\textbf{Claim.} For two-layer Haar-random $4$-local square-lattice circuits with local Hilbert-space dimension $q\ge 88$, measuring $B$ in the geometry of the paper yields extensive average post-measurement entanglement:
\[
\mathbb E_U\sum_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(\rho^A_{s_B})\ge \kappa L_x
\]
for some constant $\kappa>0$ and all sufficiently large $L_x$.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \text{Appendix-E intra-cell analysis gives a wall contribution }\|T_r\|_1\le \sqrt{d'}G_4(q)^{|W|}.\\
(P2) & \text{For }q\ge 88\text{, the same analysis gives }G_4(q)\mu_{\Lambda^*}\le e^{-\eta_4}\text{ for some }\eta_4>0.\\
(P3) & \text{The number of length-}\ell\text{ separating walks is at most }L_y\mu_{\Lambda^*}^{\ell}.\\
(P4) & \ell\ge L_x\text{ for every separating wall in the geometry}.\\
(P5) & L_y\le L_x^a\text{ for some fixed }a>0.\\
(P6) & F_4:=-\log Z_4,\quad Z_4:=\sum_W G_4(q)^{|W|}.\\
(P7) & \mathbb E_U\sum_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(\rho^A_{s_B})\ge 2F_4-2\log(eF_4)\text{ when }F_4\ge 2.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Using the counting bound,
\begin{align}
Z_4
&=\sum_W G_4(q)^{|W|} && \text{by (P6)}\\
&\le \sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}L_y\mu_{\Lambda^*}^{\ell}G_4(q)^{\ell} && \text{by (P3) and (P4)}\\
&=L_y\sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}\left(\mu_{\Lambda^*}G_4(q)\right)^{\ell} && \text{factor terms}\\
&\le L_y\sum_{\ell=L_x}^{\infty}e^{-\eta_4\ell} && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=\frac{L_y e^{-\eta_4L_x}}{1-e^{-\eta_4}}. && \text{geometric series}
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
F_4
&=-\log Z_4 && \text{by (P6)}\\
&\ge \eta_4L_x-\log L_y+\log(1-e^{-\eta_4}) && \text{take }-\log\\
&\ge \eta_4L_x-a\log L_x+\log(1-e^{-\eta_4}) && \text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
Thus $F_4\ge 2$ for sufficiently large $L_x$. Applying the optimized lower bound gives
\begin{align}
\mathbb E_U\sum_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(\rho^A_{s_B})
&\ge 2F_4-2\log(eF_4) && \text{by (P7)}\\
&\ge 2\eta_4L_x-2a\log L_x+2\log(1-e^{-\eta_4})-2\log(eF_4). && \text{substitute the bound on }F_4
\end{align}
All terms except $2\eta_4L_x$ are sublinear in $L_x$, so for sufficiently large $L_x$ the right-hand side is at least $\eta_4L_x$. Setting $\kappa:=\eta_4$ proves the claimed extensive lower bound.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{q\ge 88\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathbb E_U\sum_{s_B}p_{s_B}S(\rho^A_{s_B})\ge \kappa L_x\text{ for some }\kappa>0.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
